news.title: Wasted Wind and Solar Power Could Run Factories and Data Centers
news.summary: As the scale and reach of variable renewable energies expand around the world, more and more clean energy is being produced. However, more and more of that clean energy is also going to waste. In order to balance energy supply and demand, electric utilities rely on a process called curtailment, where they deliberately reduce the amount of energy produced by solar and wind farms in order to not overwhelm the energy grid. But a new MIT study asks: what if that excess clean energy could be used to power some of the United States’ dirtiest sectors?…

analysis.summary: An MIT study explores using curtailed wind and solar electricity to power U.S. factories and data centers.
analysis.rationale: The article discusses electricity grid curtailment and industrial power use rather than crude oil supply or demand, providing no clear directional implication for oil prices.

news.title: Oil Surge Pushes Indonesia to Mull First Subsidized Fuel Price Hike in Years
news.summary: Indonesia, the largest economy in Southeast Asia, has discussed hiking the price of subsidized fuel for the first time since 2022, as the weakening local currency and persistently high oil prices weigh on government outlays for funding the subsidies. Indonesia, the world’s fourth-most populous country, hasn’t removed or reduced subsidies for gasoline and fuel amid the Strait of Hormuz crisis. The country, a net oil importer despite having domestic oil production, has subsidized fuel in one form or another since it gained independence…

analysis.summary: Indonesia is considering its first subsidized fuel price hike since 2022 due to high oil prices and a weak currency.
analysis.rationale: Higher retail fuel prices in a major net oil importer could curb fuel demand, creating modest downward pressure on oil, though the measure is only under discussion and is a reaction to existing high prices.

news.title: Butcher blames costs for closure after 127 years
news.summary: Bennett Butchers in Spalding says rises in National Insurance and energy have made it "unviable".

analysis.summary: A 127-year-old UK butcher is closing, citing higher National Insurance and energy costs.
analysis.rationale: The closure of a single local retail business in the UK has no material implication for global crude oil supply or demand, and the text does not specify oil-specific cost drivers.
